content:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: P1 — cluster-west-1: repeated node drains detected on GPU pool 'inference-prod'. Paging on-call.
sarah: I’m on it. seeing repeated node_drain events across 3 nodes (gpu-node-12/14/19). taking ownership. any customer impact yet?

mike: There were ~4 5xxs on the API in the last 10m, mostly short-lived. GA trace shows timeouts hitting 10s while a few batches got rescheduled. linking logs: http://logs/redwood/cluster-west-1/drain-1999990000

vishal: I'm seeing spike in node_ecc_errors_total on gpu-node-19, then kernel OOMs on node-14. GPU memory pressure looks correlated: gpu_memory_used_bytes / gpu_memory_total_bytes near 0.98 for bigger models.

emily: FYI one customer (acct acme-ops) reported a few failed requests and elevated error rates — CS is monitoring.

sarah: immediate mitigation: cordon gpu-node-19 and drain it gracefully to stop flapping. increasing eviction grace to 90s for the drain. will route new traffic off that pool if drains continue.

mike: +1. Also disabling autoscheduler placement for large-batch jobs to avoid packing into remaining nodes. set node-selector to avoid cluster-west-1 for canary traffic.

vishal: tracing into telemetry: short ECC bursts (node_ecc_errors_total delta > 0) are currently alerting at 1m window which is noisy. during this incident it's firing repeatedly and causing cascading actions. recommend suppressing ECC pager and treating as alert-only until we stabilize.

sarah: Agreed. Temporarily mute alert: Prometheus rule 'GPU_ECC_BURST_PAGER' --> silence for 2h. I'll create a follow-up to revisit thresholding.

jess: Can we adjust VRAM OOM alert too? Right now ALERT_GPU_VRAM_CRITICAL fires for gpu_memory_used_percent > 95 for 5m. With a few large models we get spikes for short bursts. Propose >98 for 10m to reduce noise.

mike: That sounds reasonable. Proposed changes (quick patch):

```yaml
# prometheus/rules/gpu_alerts.yaml (proposed hotfix)
- alert: GPU_VRAM_CRITICAL
  expr: (gpu_memory_used_bytes / gpu_memory_total_bytes) * 100 > 98
  for: 10m
  labels:
    severity: critical
  annotations:
    summary: "GPU VRAM >98% for 10m on {{ $labels.instance }}"

- alert: GPU_ECC_BURST_PAGER
  expr: increase(node_ecc_errors_total[5m]) > 3
  for: 15m
  labels:
    severity: warning
  annotations:
    summary: "ECC errors >3 in 5m on {{ $labels.instance }}"
```

sarah: Applying the silence for ECC now and rolling the prometheus hotfix to reduce VRAM sensitivity.

incident-bot: Silence applied to 'GPU_ECC_BURST_PAGER' for 2h by sarah.

vishal: After cordon/drain, gpu-node-19 shows a thermal transient too: gpu_temperature_celsius spiked to 90C briefly then cooled. we should check cooling loop for that rack.

emily: Customer impact summary for CS: ~0.3% of requests from acme-ops experienced a 502/timeout window between 1999990020-1999990110. no data loss, retries succeeded. CS will send an incident note if any customer asks.

mike: Noted. I'm also creating a short-term scheduler rule to avoid binpacking of big-model pods onto the same node. This will reduce memory spikes while we rebuild nodes.

sarah: ok nodes drained. two nodes reprovisioning, one flagged for hardware inspection. moving to recovery state. handing off to vishal for follow-up OS/kernel diagnostics.

vishal: taking post-incident. next steps I'm filing: TICKET-4812 (hardware inspection for gpu-node-14/19), TICKET-4813 (cooling rack check and telemetry validation), TICKET-4814 (alert tuning: ECC window and VRAM thresholds), TICKET-4815 (dashboard: add 5m rolling VRAM P95 tile and node_drain event heatmap).

jess: please include runbook changes: add a note to not auto-evict on short ECC bursts and to prefer cordon+drain for suspected HW flaps. Also add example prom rules and expected signal windows.

mike: created PR with hotfix and ticket refs: https://git/repo/pull/7234 — will merge once SARAH confirms no regressions.

sarah: merged and Prometheus reload succeeded. I’ll unmute ECC after we’ve confirmed stability (ETA 2h).

incident-bot: P1 de-escalated to P2 by sarah — cluster health improving, no ongoing drains.

emily: CS: monitoring ACME and flagged customers for potential follow-up. if anyone wants to DM for a summary I can prepare a short timeline.

vishal: For the longer-term: propose we change the GPU alerting strategy to use multi-signal heuristics instead of single metric thresholds. e.g., alerts fire only when VRAM>threshold AND sustained OOMs OR eviction_count rising. I'll sketch a proposal in TICKET-4814.

jess: good. also suggest a new dashboard card: 'GPU Risk Score' combining temp, ECC, OOM, and drain rate so on-call can triage quickly.

sarah: thanks everyone. I'll add a short incident summary in #postmortems and assign follow-ups.

mike: small note for the follow-up: tweak the alert aggregation from 1m to 5m for node-level signals to avoid flutter.

sarah: last check: system stable, traffic back to normal. closing this pager thread. follow-ups: TICKET-4812,4813,4814,4815 assigned to eng-sre/runtime.

incident-bot: Thread closed by sarah at 1999990462."
